claim: Stellate cells (SCs) in the medial entorhinal cortex exhibit correspondence between grid cell spatial scales and their synaptic integrative properties.
source: This is exemplified by correspondence between grid cell spatial scales and the synaptic integrative properties of stellate cells (SCs) in the medial entorhinal cortex.
evidence: The abstract states this as a known relationship that motivates the study.

claim: Integrative properties of stellate cells vary between mice.
source: Using ex-vivo patch-clamp recordings from up to 55 SCs per mouse, we found that integrative properties vary between mice
evidence: The abstract presents this as a primary finding from the experimental data.

claim: Integrative properties of stellate cells have a continuous dorsoventral organization, in contrast to the modularity of grid cell spatial scales.
source: Using ex-vivo patch-clamp recordings from up to 55 SCs per mouse, we found that integrative properties vary between mice and, in contrast to the modularity of grid cell spatial scales, have a continuous dorsoventral organization.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a primary finding from the experimental data.

claim: The results constrain mechanisms for modular grid firing.
source: Our results constrain mechanisms for modular grid firing and provide evidence for inter-animal phenotypic variability among neurons of the same type.
evidence: The abstract presents this as an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: There is inter-animal phenotypic variability among neurons of the same type.
source: Our results constrain mechanisms for modular grid firing and provide evidence for inter-animal phenotypic variability among neurons of the same type.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a primary finding from the experimental data.

claim: Neuron type properties are tuned to circuit-level set points that vary within and between animals.
source: We suggest that neuron type properties are tuned to circuit-level set points that vary within and between animals.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The concept of cell types provides a general organizing principle for understanding biological structures including the brain.
source: The concept of cell types provides a general organizing principle for understanding biological structures including the brain (Regev et al., 2017; Zeng and Sanes, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Some neuronal cell types may be conceived as clustering along a line rather than around a point in a feature space.
source: The simplest conceptualization of a neuronal cell type, as a population of phenotypically similar neurons with features that cluster around a single set point (Wang et al., 2011b), is extended by observations of variability in cell type features, suggesting that some neuronal cell types may be conceived as clustering along a line rather than around a point in a feature space (Cembrowski and Menon, 2018; O'Donnell and Nolan, 2011; Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Correlations between the functional organization of sensory, motor and cognitive circuits and the electrophysiological properties of individual neuronal cell types suggest that feature variability underlies key neural computations.
source: Correlations between the functional organization of sensory, motor and cognitive circuits and the electrophysiological properties of individual neuronal cell types suggest that this feature variability underlies key neural computations (Adamson et al., 2002; Angelo et al., 2012; Fletcher and Williams, 2019; Garden et al., 2008; Giocomo et al., 2007; Kuba et al., 2005; O'Donnell and Nolan, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Within-cell type variability has typically been deduced by combining data obtained from multiple animals.
source: However, within-cell type variability has typically been deduced by combining data obtained from multiple animals.
evidence: This is presented as an observation about the state of the field.

claim: The structure of variation within individual animals or between different animals has received little attention.
source: By contrast, the structure of variation within individual animals or between different animals has received little attention.
evidence: This is presented as an observation about the state of the field.

claim: Investigations of invertebrate nervous systems show that set points may differ between animals.
source: Moreover, although investigations of invertebrate nervous systems show that set points may differ between animals (Goaillard et al., 2009), it is not clear whether mammalian neurons exhibit similar phenotypic diversity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: It is not clear whether mammalian neurons exhibit phenotypic diversity similar to invertebrate neurons.
source: Moreover, although investigations of invertebrate nervous systems show that set points may differ between animals (Goaillard et al., 2009), it is not clear whether mammalian neurons exhibit similar phenotypic diversity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is presented as a gap in knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: Distinguishing between continuous and modular organization of cell type properties requires many more electrophysiological observations for each animal than are obtained in typical studies.
source: Distinguishing these possibilities requires many more electrophysiological observations for each animal than are obtained in typical studies.
evidence: This is presented as a logical inference about experimental requirements.

claim: The MEC contains neurons that encode an animal's location through grid-like firing fields.
source: The MEC contains neurons that encode an animal's location through grid-like firing fields (Fyhn et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: The spatial scale of grid fields follows a dorsoventral organization.
source: The spatial scale of grid fields follows a dorsoventral organization (Hafting et al., 2005), which is mirrored by a dorsoventral organization in key electrophysiological features of SCs (Boehlen et al., 2010; Dodson et al., 2011; Garden et al., 2008; Giocomo et al., 2007; Giocomo and Hasselmo, 2008a; Pastoll et al., 2012a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The dorsoventral organization of grid field spatial scale is mirrored by a dorsoventral organization in key electrophysiological features of SCs.
source: The spatial scale of grid fields follows a dorsoventral organization (Hafting et al., 2005), which is mirrored by a dorsoventral organization in key electrophysiological features of SCs (Boehlen et al., 2010; Dodson et al., 2011; Garden et al., 2008; Giocomo et al., 2007; Giocomo and Hasselmo, 2008a; Pastoll et al., 2012a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Grid cells are organized into discrete modules.
source: Grid cells are further organized into discrete modules (Stensola et al., 2012), with the cells within a module having a similar grid scale and orientation (Barry et al., 2007; Gu et al., 2018; Stensola et al., 2012; Yoon et al., 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Cells within a grid module have a similar grid scale and orientation.
source: Grid cells are further organized into discrete modules (Stensola et al., 2012), with the cells within a module having a similar grid scale and orientation (Barry et al., 2007; Gu et al., 2018; Stensola et al., 2012; Yoon et al., 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Progressively more ventral grid modules are composed of cells with wider grid spacing.
source: progressively more ventral modules are composed of cells with wider grid spacing (Stensola et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Studies that demonstrate dorsoventral organization of integrative properties of SCs have relied on pooling relatively few measurements per animal.
source: Studies that demonstrate dorsoventral organization of integrative properties of SCs have so far relied on the pooling of relatively few measurements per animal.
evidence: This is presented as an observation about previous research methods.

claim: It is unclear whether the organization of cellular properties of SCs is modular.
source: Hence, it is unclear whether the organization of these cellular properties is modular, as one might expect if they directly set the scale of grid firing fields in individual grid cells (Giocomo et al., 2007).
evidence: This is presented as a gap in knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: The possibility that set points for electrophysiological properties of SCs differ between animals has not been considered previously.
source: The possibility that set points for electrophysiological properties of SCs differ between animals has also not been considered previously.
evidence: This is presented as a gap in knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: The authors introduce a modification of the gap statistic algorithm to facilitate detection of modularity using relatively few observations.
source: Because tests of whether data arise from modular as opposed to continuous distributions have received less general attention, to facilitate detection of modularity using relatively few observations, we introduce a modification of the gap statistic algorithm (Tibshirani et al., 2001) that estimates the number of modes in a dataset while controlling for observations expected by chance (see 'Materials and methods' and Figure 1—figure supplements 1–5).
evidence: This is presented as a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The modified gap statistic algorithm performs well compared with discreteness metrics based on the standard deviation of binned data.
source: This algorithm performs well compared with discreteness metrics that are based on the standard deviation of binned data (Giocomo et al., 2014; Stensola et al., 2012), which we find are prone to high false-positive rates (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Discreteness metrics based on the standard deviation of binned data are prone to high false-positive rates.
source: This algorithm performs well compared with discreteness metrics that are based on the standard deviation of binned data (Giocomo et al., 2014; Stensola et al., 2012), which we find are prone to high false-positive rates (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Recordings from approximately 30 SCs per animal should be sufficient to detect modularity using the modified gap statistic algorithm given the experimentally observed separation between grid modules.
source: We find that recordings from approximately 30 SCs per animal should be sufficient to detect modularity using the modified gap statistic algorithm and given the experimentally observed separation between grid modules (see 'Materials and methods' and Figure 1—figure supplements 2–3).
evidence: This is based on simulations and analyses presented in the Materials and methods and supplementary figures.

claim: Typically fewer than five recordings per animal were made in previous studies of SCs.
source: Although methods for high-quality recording from SCs in ex-vivo brain slices are well established (Pastoll et al., 2012b), typically fewer than five recordings per animal were made in previous studies, which is many fewer than our estimate of the minimum number of observations required to test for modularity.
evidence: This is presented as an observation about previous research methods.

claim: The authors measured electrophysiological features of 836 SCs from 27 mice.
source: With these procedures, we measured and analyzed electrophysiological features of 836 SCs (n/mouse: range 11–55; median = 35) from 27 mice (median age = 37 days, age range = 18–57 days).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental dataset.

claim: The median number of SCs recorded per mouse was 35.
source: With these procedures, we measured and analyzed electrophysiological features of 836 SCs (n/mouse: range 11–55; median = 35) from 27 mice (median age = 37 days, age range = 18–57 days).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental dataset.

claim: The median age of mice was 37 days with an age range of 18–57 days.
source: With these procedures, we measured and analyzed electrophysiological features of 836 SCs (n/mouse: range 11–55; median = 35) from 27 mice (median age = 37 days, age range = 18–57 days).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental dataset.

claim: Some mice were housed in a standard home cage with dimensions 0.2 × 0.37 m.
source: The mice were housed either in a standard home cage (dimensions: 0.2 × 0.37 m, N = 18 mice, n = 583 neurons) or from postnatal day 16 in a 2.4 × 1.2 m cage, which provided a large environment that could be freely explored (N = 9, n = 253, median age = 38 days) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental conditions.

claim: Some mice were housed from postnatal day 16 in a 2.4 × 1.2 m cage that provided a large environment that could be freely explored.
source: The mice were housed either in a standard home cage (dimensions: 0.2 × 0.37 m, N = 18 mice, n = 583 neurons) or from postnatal day 16 in a 2.4 × 1.2 m cage, which provided a large environment that could be freely explored (N = 9, n = 253, median age = 38 days) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental conditions.

claim: The authors measured six sub-threshold integrative properties for each neuron.
source: For each neuron, we measured six sub-threshold integrative properties (Figure 2A–B) and six supra-threshold integrative properties (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental measurements, with reference to Figure 2.

claim: The authors measured six supra-threshold integrative properties for each neuron.
source: For each neuron, we measured six sub-threshold integrative properties (Figure 2A–B) and six supra-threshold integrative properties (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental measurements, with reference to Figure 2.

claim: SCs are found intermingled with pyramidal cells in layer 2 (L2PCs).
source: Because SCs are found intermingled with pyramidal cells in layer 2 (L2PCs), and as misclassification of L2PCs as SCs would probably confound investigation of intra-SC variation, we validated our criteria for distinguishing each cell type.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the anatomy of the MEC.

claim: The authors identified two populations of neurons in layer 2 of MEC that were labelled in Wfs1Cre mice.
source: We identified two populations of neurons in layer 2 of MEC that were labelled in Wfs1Cre mice (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 3.

claim: The more numerous population of Wfs1Cre-labeled neurons had properties consistent with L2PCs.
source: The more numerous population had properties consistent with L2PCs (Figure 3A,G) and could be separated from the unidentified population on the basis of a lower rheobase (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 3.

claim: The L2PC and unidentified populations could be separated on the basis of rheobase.
source: The more numerous population had properties consistent with L2PCs (Figure 3A,G) and could be separated from the unidentified population on the basis of a lower rheobase (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 3.

claim: The unidentified population of Wfs1Cre-labeled neurons had firing properties typical of layer 2 interneurons.
source: The unidentified population had firing properties that were typical of layer 2 interneurons (Gonzalez-Sulser et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: A principal component analysis clearly separated the L2PC population from the SC population.
source: A principal component analysis (PCA) (Figure 3D–F) clearly separated the L2PC population from the SC population, but did not identify subpopulations of SCs.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 3.

claim: Principal component analysis did not identify subpopulations of SCs.
source: A principal component analysis (PCA) (Figure 3D–F) clearly separated the L2PC population from the SC population, but did not identify subpopulations of SCs.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 3.

claim: The SC population used for analyses is distinct from other cell types found in layer 2 of the MEC.
source: These data demonstrate that the SC population used for our analyses is distinct from other cell types also found in layer 2 of the MEC.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the PCA and other analyses.

claim: There are substantial dorsoventral gradients in input resistance, sag, membrane time constant, resonant frequency, rheobase and the current-frequency relationship in SCs.
source: We found substantial (adjusted R2 >0.1) dorsoventral gradients in input resistance, sag, membrane time constant, resonant frequency, rheobase and the current-frequency (I-F) relationship (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 3G.

claim: There is no evidence for dorsoventral organization of electrophysiological features in L2PCs.
source: In contrast to the situation in SCs, we did not find evidence for dorsoventral organization of these features in L2PCs (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 3G.

claim: The large dataset replicates the previously observed dependence of integrative properties of SCs on their dorsoventral position.
source: Thus, our large dataset replicates the previously observed dependence of integrative properties of SCs on their dorsoventral position, and shows that this location dependence further distinguishes SCs from L2PCs.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: Location dependence of integrative properties further distinguishes SCs from L2PCs.
source: Thus, our large dataset replicates the previously observed dependence of integrative properties of SCs on their dorsoventral position, and shows that this location dependence further distinguishes SCs from L2PCs.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: Distributions of some features of SCs from different animals could be almost completely non-overlapping despite consistent and strong dorsoventral tuning.
source: Comparing specific features between individual animals suggested that their distributions could be almost completely non-overlapping, despite consistent and strong dorsoventral tuning (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 4A.

claim: Mixed models for all electrophysiological features gave a substantially better fit to the data than linear models that considered all neurons as independent.
source: Consistent with this, we found that mixed models for all electrophysiological features gave a substantially better fit to the data than linear models that considered all neurons as independent (adjusted p<2×10−17 for all models, χ2 test, Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results, with reference to Table 1.

claim: For properties with substantial dorsoventral tuning, the conditional R2 value for the mixed effect model was substantially larger than the marginal R2 value.
source: Furthermore, even for properties with substantial (R2 value >0.1) dorsoventral tuning, the conditional R2 value for the mixed effect model was substantially larger than the marginal R2 value (Figure 4D and Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results, with reference to Figure 4D and Table 1.

claim: The analyses demonstrate inter-animal variability in key electrophysiological features of SCs.
source: Together, these analyses demonstrate inter-animal variability in key electrophysiological features of SCs, suggesting that the set points that establish the underlying integrative properties differ between animals.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the statistical analyses.

claim: The set points that establish the underlying integrative properties of SCs differ between animals.
source: Together, these analyses demonstrate inter-animal variability in key electrophysiological features of SCs, suggesting that the set points that establish the underlying integrative properties differ between animals.
evidence: This is presented as an inference from the inter-animal variability findings.

claim: Neuronal integrative properties may be modified by changes in neural activity.
source: Because neuronal integrative properties may be modified by changes in neural activity (Zhang and Linden, 2003), we asked whether experience influences the measured electrophysiological features of SCs.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Standard mouse housing has dimensions less than the distance between the firing fields of more ventrally located grid cells.
source: As standard mouse housing has dimensions less than the distance between the firing fields of more ventrally located grid cells (Brun et al., 2008; Hafting et al., 2005), in a standard home cage, only a relatively small fraction of ventral grid cells is likely to be activated, whereas larger housing should lead to the activation of a greater proportion of ventral grid cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: In a standard home cage, only a relatively small fraction of ventral grid cells is likely to be activated.
source: As standard mouse housing has dimensions less than the distance between the firing fields of more ventrally located grid cells (Brun et al., 2008; Hafting et al., 2005), in a standard home cage, only a relatively small fraction of ventral grid cells is likely to be activated, whereas larger housing should lead to the activation of a greater proportion of ventral grid cells.
evidence: This is presented as a logical inference from the relationship between housing size and grid cell properties.

claim: Larger housing should lead to the activation of a greater proportion of ventral grid cells.
source: As standard mouse housing has dimensions less than the distance between the firing fields of more ventrally located grid cells (Brun et al., 2008; Hafting et al., 2005), in a standard home cage, only a relatively small fraction of ventral grid cells is likely to be activated, whereas larger housing should lead to the activation of a greater proportion of ventral grid cells.
evidence: This is presented as a logical inference from the relationship between housing size and grid cell properties.

claim: Larger housing was associated with a smaller sag coefficient, indicating an increased sag response.
source: We found that larger housing was associated with a smaller sag coefficient, indicating an increased sag response, a lower resonant frequency and a larger spike half-width (adjusted p<0.05; Figure 4E, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings.

claim: Larger housing was associated with a lower resonant frequency.
source: We found that larger housing was associated with a smaller sag coefficient, indicating an increased sag response, a lower resonant frequency and a larger spike half-width (adjusted p<0.05; Figure 4E, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings.

claim: Larger housing was associated with a larger spike half-width.
source: We found that larger housing was associated with a smaller sag coefficient, indicating an increased sag response, a lower resonant frequency and a larger spike half-width (adjusted p<0.05; Figure 4E, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings.

claim: Housing-related differences in SC properties were primarily from changes to the magnitude rather than the location-dependence of each feature.
source: These differences were primarily from changes to the magnitude rather than the location-dependence of each feature.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings.

claim: Mixed models incorporating animal identity continued to provide a better account of the data after accounting for housing.
source: To determine whether inter-animal differences remain after accounting for housing, we compared mixed models that include dorsoventral location and housing as fixed effects with equivalent linear regression models in which individual animals were not accounted for. Mixed models incorporating animal identity continued to provide a better account of the data, both for features that were dependent on housing (adjusted p<2.8×10−21) and for features that were not (adjusted p<1.4×10−7) (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Specific electrophysiological features of SCs may be modified by experience of large environments.
source: Together, these data suggest that specific electrophysiological features of SCs may be modified by experience of large environments.
evidence: This is presented as an inference from the housing experiment findings.

claim: After accounting for housing, significant inter-animal variation remains in SC properties.
source: After accounting for housing, significant inter-animal variation remains, suggesting that additional mechanisms acting at the level of animals rather than individual neurons also determine differences between SCs.
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Additional mechanisms acting at the level of animals rather than individual neurons determine differences between SCs.
source: After accounting for housing, significant inter-animal variation remains, suggesting that additional mechanisms acting at the level of animals rather than individual neurons also determine differences between SCs.
evidence: This is presented as an inference from the persistence of inter-animal variation after accounting for housing.

claim: Properties related to the action potential waveform depended on the mediolateral position of the recorded neuron.
source: Several of the variables influenced some measured electrophysiological features, for example properties primarily related to the action potential waveform depended on the mediolateral position of the recorded neuron (Supplementary file 6; Canto and Witter, 2012; Yoshida et al., 2013), but significant inter-animal differences remained after accounting for each variable.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, supported by citations.

claim: Significant inter-animal differences remained after accounting for experimental and biological variables including home cage size, brain hemisphere, mediolateral position, experimenter identity, and time since slice preparation.
source: To address the possibility that other experimental or biological variables could contribute to inter-animal differences, we evaluated the effects of home cage size (Supplementary files 3–4), brain hemisphere (Supplementary file 5), mediolateral position (Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 6), the identity of the experimenter (Supplementary file 7) and time since slice preparation (Supplementary files 8 and 9). Several of the variables influenced some measured electrophysiological features, for example properties primarily related to the action potential waveform depended on the mediolateral position of the recorded neuron (Supplementary file 6; Canto and Witter, 2012; Yoshida et al., 2013), but significant inter-animal differences remained after accounting for each variable.
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The majority (10/12) of the electrophysiological features were not significantly associated with the number of recorded neurons.
source: However, the majority (10/12) of the electrophysiological features were not significantly (p>0.2) associated with the number of recorded neurons (Supplementary file 12).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Analyses of inter-animal differences focusing only on data from animals with >35 recordings are consistent with conclusions from analysis of the larger dataset.
source: Second, analyses of inter-animal differences that focus only on data from animals for which >35 recordings were made, which should only be feasible with uniformly high-quality brain slices, are consistent with conclusions from analysis of the larger dataset (Supplementary file 13).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The conditional R2 values of electrophysiological features of L2PCs are much lower than those for SCs recorded under the same experimental conditions.
source: Third, the conditional R2 values of electrophysiological features of L2PCs are much lower than those for SCs recorded under the same experimental conditions (Table 1 and Supplementary file 1), suggesting that inter-animal variation may be specific to SCs and cannot be explained by slice conditions.
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Inter-animal variation may be specific to SCs and cannot be explained by slice conditions.
source: Third, the conditional R2 values of electrophysiological features of L2PCs are much lower than those for SCs recorded under the same experimental conditions (Table 1 and Supplementary file 1), suggesting that inter-animal variation may be specific to SCs and cannot be explained by slice conditions.
evidence: This is presented as an inference from the comparison of conditional R2 values between SCs and L2PCs.

claim: Differences between animals remain after accounting for experimental and technical factors that might contribute to variation in the measured features of SCs.
source: Together, these analyses indicate that differences between animals remain after accounting for experimental and technical factors that might contribute to variation in the measured features of SCs.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from multiple analyses.

claim: For datasets with n ≥ 34 SCs, if properties are modular, this would be detected by the modified gap statistic in at least 50% of animals.
source: For n ≥ 34 SCs, we expect that if properties are modular, then this would be detected by the modified gap statistic in at least 50% of animals (Figure 1—figure supplements 2C and 3).
evidence: This is based on simulations presented in the supplementary figures.

claim: For datasets from the majority of animals, the modified gap statistic identifies only a single mode in the distribution of rheobase values.
source: By contrast, we find that for datasets from the majority of animals, the modified gap statistic identifies only a single mode in the distribution of rheobase values (Figure 5A and Figure 6) (N = 13/15)
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figures 5A and 6.

claim: For datasets from the majority of animals, the modified gap statistic identifies only a single mode in the distribution of resonant frequencies.
source: By contrast, we find that for datasets from the majority of animals, the modified gap statistic identifies only a single mode in the distribution of rheobase values (Figure 5A and Figure 6) (N = 13/15) and of resonant frequencies (Figure 5B and Figure 6) (N = 14/15), indicating that these properties have a continuous rather than a modular distribution.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figures 5B and 6.

claim: Rheobase and resonant frequency of SCs have a continuous rather than a modular distribution.
source: By contrast, we find that for datasets from the majority of animals, the modified gap statistic identifies only a single mode in the distribution of rheobase values (Figure 5A and Figure 6) (N = 13/15) and of resonant frequencies (Figure 5B and Figure 6) (N = 14/15), indicating that these properties have a continuous rather than a modular distribution.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the gap statistic analysis.

claim: The rheobase and resonant frequency of SCs, although depending strongly on a neuron's dorsoventral position, do not have a detectable modular organization.
source: Thus, the rheobase and resonant frequency of SCs, although depending strongly on a neuron's dorsoventral position, do not have a detectable modular organization.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the gap statistic analysis.

claim: Across all properties, for any given property, at most 3 out of 15 mice were evaluated as having a clustered organization using the modified gap statistic.
source: Across all properties, for any given property, at most 3 out of 15 mice were evaluated as having a clustered organization using the modified gap statistic (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 6.

claim: The proportion of datasets evaluated as modular does not differ significantly from the proportion expected by chance when no modularity is present.
source: This does not differ significantly from the proportion expected by chance when no modularity is present (p>0.05, binomial test).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The average proportion of datasets evaluated as modular across all measured features was 0.072 ± 0.02.
source: Consistent with this, the average proportion of datasets evaluated as modular across all measured features was 0.072 ± 0.02 (± SEM), which is similar to the expected false-positive rate.
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The properties of grid firing fields previously recorded with tetrodes in behaving animals were detected as having a modular organization using the modified gap statistic.
source: By contrast, the properties of grid firing fields previously recorded with tetrodes in behaving animals (Stensola et al., 2012) were detected as having a modular organization using the modified gap statistic (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a direct statement of analysis results applied to previously published data.

claim: It is unlikely that any of the intrinsic integrative properties of SCs examined have organization within individual animals resembling the modular organization of grid cells in behaving animals.
source: Therefore, we conclude that it is unlikely that any of the intrinsic integrative properties of SCs that we examined have organization within individual animals resembling the modular organization of grid cells in behaving animals.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the gap statistic analyses.

claim: Many of the measured electrophysiological features of SCs emerge from shared ionic mechanisms.
source: Finally, because many of the measured electrophysiological features of SCs emerge from shared ionic mechanisms (Dodson et al., 2011; Garden et al., 2008; Pastoll et al., 2012a), we asked whether dorsoventral tuning reflects a single core mechanism and whether inter-animal differences are specific to this mechanism or manifest more generally.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The first five dimensions of a principal components analysis of all measured electrophysiological features accounted for almost 80% of the variance.
source: The first five dimensions of a principal components analysis (PCA) of all measured electrophysiological features accounted for almost 80% of the variance (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results, with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: The first two principal components depended significantly on dorsoventral location.
source: When we fit the principal components using mixed models with location as a fixed effect and animal identity as a random effect, we found that the first two components depended significantly on dorsoventral location (Figure 7E and Supplementary file 14) (marginal R2 = 0.50 and 0.09 and adjusted p=1.09×10−15 and 1.05 × 10−4, respectively).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The dependence of multiple electrophysiological features on dorsoventral position may be reducible to two core mechanisms that together account for much of the variability between SCs in their intrinsic electrophysiology.
source: Thus, the dependence of multiple electrophysiological features on dorsoventral position may be reducible to two core mechanisms that together account for much of the variability between SCs in their intrinsic electrophysiology.
evidence: This is presented as an inference from the PCA results.

claim: The intercept, but not the slope of the dependence of the first two principal components on dorsoventral position depended on housing.
source: The intercept, but not the slope of the dependence of the first two principal components on dorsoventral position depended on housing (adjusted p=0.039 and 0.027) (Figure 7E,F and Supplementary file 15).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: After accounting for housing, the first two principal components were still better fit by models that include animal identity as a random effect.
source: After accounting for housing, the first two principal components were still better fit by models that include animal identity as a random effect (adjusted p=3.3×10−9 and 4.1 × 10−86), indicating remaining inter-animal differences in these components (Supplementary file 16).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Nine of the next ten higher-order principal components did not depend on housing.
source: A further nine of the next ten higher-order principal components did not depend on housing (adjusted p>0.1) (Supplementary file 15), while eight differed significantly between animals (adjusted p<0.05) (Supplementary file 16).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Eight of the next ten higher-order principal components differed significantly between animals.
source: A further nine of the next ten higher-order principal components did not depend on housing (adjusted p>0.1) (Supplementary file 15), while eight differed significantly between animals (adjusted p<0.05) (Supplementary file 16).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The dorsoventral organization of multiple electrophysiological features of SCs is captured by two principal components, suggesting two main sources of variance.
source: Together, these analyses indicate that the dorsoventral organization of multiple electrophysiological features of SCs is captured by two principal components, suggesting two main sources of variance, both of which are dependent on experience.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the PCA analyses.

claim: Both main sources of variance in SC properties are dependent on experience.
source: Together, these analyses indicate that the dorsoventral organization of multiple electrophysiological features of SCs is captured by two principal components, suggesting two main sources of variance, both of which are dependent on experience.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the PCA analyses.

claim: Significant inter-animal variation in the major sources of variance remains after accounting for experience and experimental parameters.
source: Significant inter-animal variation in the major sources of variance remains after accounting for experience and experimental parameters.
evidence: This is presented as a conclusion from the PCA analyses.

claim: Phenotypic variation is found across many areas of biology but has received little attention in investigations of mammalian nervous systems.
source: Phenotypic variation is found across many areas of biology (Geiler-Samerotte et al., 2013), but has received little attention in investigations of mammalian nervous systems.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and presents an observation about the state of the field.

claim: The integrative properties of neurons are determined by set points that differ between animals and are controlled at a circuit level.
source: We find unexpected inter-animal variability in SC properties, suggesting that the integrative properties of neurons are determined by set points that differ between animals and are controlled at a circuit level (Figure 8).
evidence: This is presented as an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Continuous, location-dependent organization of set points for SC integrative properties provides new constraints on models for grid cell firing.
source: Continuous, location-dependent organization of set points for SC integrative properties provides new constraints on models for grid cell firing.
evidence: This is presented as an implication of the findings.

claim: The existence of inter-animal differences in set points has implications for experimental design.
source: More generally, the existence of inter-animal differences in set points has implications for experimental design and raises new questions about how the integrative properties of neurons are specified.
evidence: This is presented as an implication of the findings.

claim: Theoretical models suggest how different cell types can be generated by varying target concentrations of intracellular Ca2+ or rates of ion channel expression.
source: Theoretical models suggest how different cell types can be generated by varying target concentrations of intracellular Ca2+ or rates of ion channel expression (O'Leary et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: The within cell type variability predicted by theoretical models arises from different initial conditions.
source: The within cell type variability predicted by these models arises from different initial conditions and may explain the variability in our data between neurons from the same animal at the same dorsoventral location (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is presented as an interpretation based on theoretical models.

claim: The dependence of integrative properties on position and their variation between animals implies additional mechanisms that operate at the circuit level.
source: By contrast, the dependence of integrative properties on position and their variation between animals implies additional mechanisms that operate at the circuit level (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is presented as an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: Inter-animal variation in integrative properties could be accounted for by inter-animal differences in dorsoventrally tuned or spatially uniform factors that influence ion channel expression or target points for intracellular Ca2+.
source: In principle, this variation could be accounted for by inter-animal differences in dorsoventrally tuned or spatially uniform factors that influence ion channel expression or target points for intracellular Ca2+ (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is presented as a speculative explanation for the findings.

claim: In invertebrates, inter-animal variability is between properties of individual identified neurons.
source: In invertebrates, inter-animal variability is between properties of individual identified neurons (Goaillard et al., 2009), whereas in mammalian nervous systems, neurons are not individually identifiable and the variation that we describe here is at the level of cell populations.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and contrasts invertebrate and mammalian systems.

claim: In mammalian nervous systems, neurons are not individually identifiable and the variation described is at the level of cell populations.
source: In invertebrates, inter-animal variability is between properties of individual identified neurons (Goaillard et al., 2009), whereas in mammalian nervous systems, neurons are not individually identifiable and the variation that we describe here is at the level of cell populations.
evidence: This is presented as an observation about mammalian nervous systems.

claim: Granule cells in the dentate gyrus that receive input from SCs increase their excitability when animals are housed in enriched environments.
source: For example, granule cells in the dentate gyrus that receive input from SCs increase their excitability when animals are housed in enriched environments (Green and Greenough, 1986; Ohline and Abraham, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Dorsoventral gradients in the electrophysiological features of SCs have stimulated cellular models for the organization of grid firing.
source: Dorsoventral gradients in the electrophysiological features of SCs have stimulated cellular models for the organization of grid firing (Burgess, 2008; Giocomo and Hasselmo, 2008b; Grossberg and Pilly, 2012; O'Donnell and Nolan, 2011; Widloski and Fiete, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Increases in spatial scale following deletion of HCN1 channels support a relationship between the electrophysiological properties of SCs and grid cell spatial scales.
source: Increases in spatial scale following deletion of HCN1 channels (Giocomo et al., 2011), which in part determine the dorsoventral organization of SC integrative properties (Garden et al., 2008; Giocomo and Hasselmo, 2009), support a relationship between the electrophysiological properties of SCs and grid cell spatial scales.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The data argue against models that explain the relationship between SC properties and grid scales through single cell computations.
source: Our data argue against models that explain this relationship through single cell computations (Burgess, 2008; Burgess et al., 2007; Giocomo et al., 2007), as in this case, the modularity of integrative properties of SCs is required to generate modularity of grid firing.
evidence: This is presented as an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: A continuous dorsoventral organization of the electrophysiological properties of SCs could support the modular grid firing generated by self-organizing maps.
source: A continuous dorsoventral organization of the electrophysiological properties of SCs could support the modular grid firing generated by self-organizing maps (Grossberg and Pilly, 2012) or by synaptic learning mechanisms (Kropff and Treves, 2008; Urdapilleta et al., 2017).
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: A continuous dorsoventral organization of the electrophysiological properties of SCs could support the modular grid firing generated by synaptic learning mechanisms.
source: A continuous dorsoventral organization of the electrophysiological properties of SCs could support the modular grid firing generated by self-organizing maps (Grossberg and Pilly, 2012) or by synaptic learning mechanisms (Kropff and Treves, 2008; Urdapilleta et al., 2017).
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Continuous attractor network models can account for modularity by limiting synaptic interactions between modules.
source: It is less clear how a continuous gradient would affect the organization of grid firing predicted by continuous attractor network models, which can instead account for modularity by limiting synaptic interactions between modules (Burak and Fiete, 2009; Bush and Burgess, 2014; Fuhs and Touretzky, 2006; Guanella et al., 2007; Shipston-Sharman et al., 2016; Widloski and Fiete, 2014; Yoon et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Modularity of grid cell firing could arise through the anatomical clustering of calbindin-positive L2PCs.
source: Modularity of grid cell firing could also arise through the anatomical clustering of calbindin-positive L2PCs (Ray et al., 2014; Ray and Brecht, 2016).
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Many SCs do not appear to generate grid codes.
source: Because many SCs do not appear to generate grid codes and as the most abundant functional cell type in the MEC appears to be non-grid spatial neurons (Diehl et al., 2017; Hardcastle et al., 2017), the continuous dorsoventral organization of SC integrative properties may also impact grid firing indirectly through modulation of these codes.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The most abundant functional cell type in the MEC appears to be non-grid spatial neurons.
source: Because many SCs do not appear to generate grid codes and as the most abundant functional cell type in the MEC appears to be non-grid spatial neurons (Diehl et al., 2017; Hardcastle et al., 2017), the continuous dorsoventral organization of SC integrative properties may also impact grid firing indirectly through modulation of these codes.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The continuous dorsoventral organization of SC integrative properties may impact grid firing indirectly through modulation of non-grid spatial codes.
source: Because many SCs do not appear to generate grid codes and as the most abundant functional cell type in the MEC appears to be non-grid spatial neurons (Diehl et al., 2017; Hardcastle et al., 2017), the continuous dorsoventral organization of SC integrative properties may also impact grid firing indirectly through modulation of these codes.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation.

claim: The similar dorsoventral organization of subthreshold integrative properties of SCs from medial and lateral parts of the MEC appears consistent with the organization of grid cell modules recorded in behaving animals.
source: The similar dorsoventral organization of subthreshold integrative properties of SCs from medial and lateral parts of the MEC appears consistent with the organization of grid cell modules recorded in behaving animals (Stensola et al., 2012).
evidence: This is presented as an inference from the experimental findings, supported by a citation.

claim: The continuous dorsoventral variation of the electrophysiological features of SCs is consistent with continuous dorsoventral gradients in gene expression along layer 2 of the MEC.
source: The continuous dorsoventral variation of the electrophysiological features of SCs suggested by our analysis is consistent with continuous dorsoventral gradients in gene expression along layer 2 of the MEC (Ramsden et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Labelling of the mRNA and protein for the HCN1 ion channel suggests a continuous dorsoventral gradient in its expression.
source: For example, labelling of the mRNA and protein for the HCN1 ion channel suggests a continuous dorsoventral gradient in its expression (Nolan et al., 2007; Ramsden et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of other brain areas indicates that although the expression profiles for some cell types cluster around a point in feature space, others lie along a continuum.
source: It is also consistent with single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of other brain areas, which indicates that although the expression profiles for some cell types cluster around a point in feature space, others lie along a continuum (Cembrowski and Menon, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: In the crab stomatogastric ganglion, inter-animal variation correlates with circuit performance.
source: In the crab stomatogastric ganglion, inter-animal variation correlates with circuit performance (Goaillard et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Variation in intrinsic properties of SCs might correlate with differences in grid firing.
source: Accordingly, variation in intrinsic properties of SCs might correlate with differences in grid firing (Domnisoru et al., 2013; Gu et al., 2018; Rowland et al., 2018; Schmidt-Hieber and Häusser, 2013) or behaviors that rely on SCs (Kitamura et al., 2014; Qin et al., 2018; Tennant et al., 2018).
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Variation in intrinsic properties of SCs might correlate with differences in behaviors that rely on SCs.
source: Accordingly, variation in intrinsic properties of SCs might correlate with differences in grid firing (Domnisoru et al., 2013; Gu et al., 2018; Rowland et al., 2018; Schmidt-Hieber and Häusser, 2013) or behaviors that rely on SCs (Kitamura et al., 2014; Qin et al., 2018; Tennant et al., 2018).
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: There appear to be inter-animal differences in the spatial scale of grid modules.
source: It is interesting in this respect that there appear to be inter-animal differences in the spatial scale of grid modules (Figure 5 of Stensola et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Modification of grid field scaling following deletion of HCN1 channels is consistent with the possibility that variation in intrinsic properties of SCs correlates with differences in grid firing.
source: Modification of grid field scaling following deletion of HCN1 channels is also consistent with this possibility (Giocomo et al., 2011; Mallory et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Inter-animal differences may reflect multiple ways to achieve a common higher-order phenotype.
source: Alternatively, inter-animal differences may reflect multiple ways to achieve a common higher-order phenotype.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative alternative interpretation.

claim: According to one view, coding of spatial location by SCs would not differ between animals despite lower level variation in their intrinsic electrophysiological features.
source: According to this view, coding of spatial location by SCs would not differ between animals despite lower level variation in their intrinsic electrophysiological features.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation.

claim: The results identify substantial within cell type variation in neuronal integrative properties that manifests between as well as within animals.
source: In conclusion, our results identify substantial within cell type variation in neuronal integrative properties that manifests between as well as within animals.
evidence: This is presented as a summary conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: The distribution of replicates from the same animal will differ from those obtained from different animals.
source: This has implications for experimental design and model building as the distribution of replicates from the same animal will differ from those obtained from different animals (Marder and Taylor, 2011).
evidence: This is presented as an implication of the findings, supported by a citation.

claim: Many behaviors are characterized by substantial inter-animal variation.
source: Many behaviors are characterized by substantial inter-animal variation (e.g. Villette et al., 2017), which could result from variation in neuronal integrative properties, or could drive this variation.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: External factors such as social interactions may affect brain circuitry.
source: For example, it is possible that external factors such as social interactions may affect brain circuitry (Wang et al., 2011a; Wang et al., 2014), although these effects appear to be focused on frontal cortical structures rather than circuits for spatial computations (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Effects of social interactions on brain circuitry appear to be focused on frontal cortical structures rather than circuits for spatial computations.
source: For example, it is possible that external factors such as social interactions may affect brain circuitry (Wang et al., 2011a; Wang et al., 2014), although these effects appear to be focused on frontal cortical structures rather than circuits for spatial computations (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Stochastic mechanisms operating at the population level may drive the emergence of inter-animal differences during the development of SCs.
source: Alternatively, stochastic mechanisms operating at the population level may drive the emergence of inter-animal differences during the development of SCs (Donato et al., 2017; Ray and Brecht, 2016).
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: All experimental procedures were performed under a United Kingdom Home Office license and with approval of the University of Edinburgh's animal welfare committee.
source: All experimental procedures were performed under a United Kingdom Home Office license and with approval of the University of Edinburgh's animal welfare committee.
evidence: This is a direct statement of ethical compliance.

claim: Recordings of many SCs per animal used C57Bl/6J mice.
source: Recordings of many SCs per animal used C57Bl/6J mice (Charles River).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental methods.

claim: Recordings targeting calbindin cells used a Wfs1Cre line crossed to RCE:loxP reporter mice.
source: Recordings targeting calbindin cells used a Wfs1Cre line (Wfs1-Tg3-CreERT2) obtained from Jackson Labs (Strain name: B6;C3-Tg(Wfs1-cre/ERT2)3Aibs/J; stock number:009103) crossed to RCE:loxP (R26R CAG-boosted EGFP) reporter mice (described in Miyoshi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental methods.

claim: The median dorsal-ventral extent of the recorded SCs was 1644 µm.
source: The median dorsal-ventral extent of the recorded SCs was 1644 µm (range 0–2464 µm).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental data.

claim: The modified gap statistic identified clustered grid spacing for 6 of 7 animals previously identified as having grid modules and with n ≥ 20.
source: We find that the modified gap statistic identified clustered grid spacing for 6 of 7 animals previously identified as having grid modules and with n ≥ 20.
evidence: This is a direct statement of analysis results applied to previously published data.

claim: The largest spacing between contiguous grid modules in each mouse is always >5.6 standard deviations.
source: This analysis suggested that the largest spacing between contiguous modules in each mouse is always >5.6 standard deviations (mean = 20.5 ± 5.0 standard deviations).
evidence: This is a direct statement of analysis results applied to previously published data.
